paragraphs.source_en: Meitei said, “Why, you ask? Nowadays human life is precious, so the police protect it; but for the people of that age, being alive will be suffering, and so the police, out of compassion, will beat you to death. Of course, most people with a little sense will already have killed themselves, so the ones the police beat to death will be no more than miserable cowards afraid to die, or idiots and invalids incapable of suicide. So anyone who wants to be killed need only paste a notice at his gate; it is quite simple, just write: In this house there is a man or woman who wishes to be killed. The police will come around on patrol when it suits them and immediately carry out the wish. What about the corpse, you ask? The police will also come around pulling carts to collect the corpses. And still more amusing things will come to pass...”

paragraphs.source_en: Meitei said, “Indeed, indeed. This example is certainly a very useful sermon. I too can tell a story about being misled by the habits before one’s eyes. The other day I read a magazine, and in it there was a novel about a swindler. Suppose I opened a shop here for paintings, calligraphy, and antiques, and put out front several paintings by great masters or various utensils made by famous craftsmen of former days. Since they are superior goods, the prices are naturally high. Then along comes a curious customer and asks how much this Motonobu scroll is. I say, let us call it six hundred yen.
